subject: Marketplace seller VAT validation & invoice collection plan
messages:
From: Oliver James <oliver.james@arcadia-retail.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 14:12:00 +0100
Subject: VAT handling for marketplace sellers - data attached

Hi Priya,

Quick note from our finance team — we run a marketplace with mixed domestic (DE) and intra-EU sellers. We've started seeing discrepancies on VAT application across seller invoices and want Redwood's recommended process for:
- validating seller VAT IDs (VIES checks + fallback)
- when/where to apply reverse-charge vs charge VAT to end-customer
- whether Redwood can hold collection until seller VAT is validated

Attached is a small sample (seller_vat_table.csv) showing 120 sellers flagged as "unverified". Our ask: can Redwood offer a workflow to (1) auto-validate, (2) flag invoices for reverse-charge where appropriate, and (3) hold settlements/collections for sellers pending validation? Also wondering about evidence we can keep for audits (validation logs, timestamps).

We have month-end coming up; would like a plan by EOD Wed if possible. CC'ing finance@arcadia-retail.com for context.

Thanks,
Oliver James
Head of Payments
Arcadia Retail

Attachment: seller_vat_table.csv (CSV, 14KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Oliver James <oliver.james@arcadia-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:03:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: VAT handling for marketplace sellers - data attached

Thanks Oliver — good to get this. Short answer: yes, we can operationalize a validation + conditional collection flow. High-level proposal below; I'll coordinate with Ben on implementation details and loop in Evelyn for compliance text.

Proposed 5-step workflow (draft):
1) Intake: seller VAT ID captured at onboarding + tiled into billing metadata (seller.vat_id).
2) Auto-validate: nightly VIES check + regex sanitization. Valid IDs flag seller.status = "vat_valid".
3) Fallback review: automated false-positives go into a human queue (Maya from your external tax advisor can be looped).
4) Billing application: when seller.vat_valid == true AND buyer.country != seller.country (EU cross-border B2B), mark line-item as reverse-charge (0% VAT on platform invoice) and include seller VAT ID + reverse-charge note on invoice. Otherwise charge VAT.
5) Collection hold: optionally place settlements into "pending_validation" state for up to N days (configurable, default 7 business days) — funds are not remitted to sellers until validation completes. Redwood will still show an invoice to buyer but include audit trail notes.

Questions/notes:
- We will keep validation logs (timestamp, VIES response, IP, operator) and can expose them via the Console and API for audits.
- Need agreement on collection hold windows and revenue recognition impact — flags for finance teams.
- There are UX impacts for sellers (notifications, appeals) that we should scope.

Ben — can you outline the expected config knobs and effort to support invoice line splitting + per-seller VAT metadata? Evelyn — any immediate compliance must-haves to surface to the customer?

I'll draft an executive summary doc and a sample invoice template after we confirm.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-vat-policy-draft.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver James <oliver.james@arcadia-retail.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:18:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: VAT handling for marketplace sellers - data attached

Thanks — tagging on technical feasibility and a proposed implementation pattern.

Implementation notes (summary):
- Metadata capture: we already support free-form invoice metadata. We'll add a standard key seller.vat_id and seller.vat_valid (boolean) at settlement time.
- VIES integration: lightweight nightly batch that hits VIES and persists the response. We can expose VIES status via the Billing API.
- Invoice splitting: platform invoice can contain line-items per underlying seller with seller-id and VAT flag per line. For bookkeeping, we will also emit a per-seller settlement record (csv/json) for your ledger.
- Reverse-charge flag: implement as a line-level tax_rate = 0 and tax_note = "Reverse charge (Article 194) - seller VAT ID: <value>". This will be visible on PDF invoices and the API.
- Collection hold: we can add a 'validation_hold' state to settlements; holds will prevent automatic payout jobs and can be overridden manually. Default TTL 7 business days; config via account settings.

Performance/ops considerations:
- Holding settlements increases the size of outstanding balance queues and will slightly increase memory footprint for the payout service; impact is marginal at low volumes but could require tuning at scale.
- For monthly consolidated invoices, we can still include per-seller VAT lines but will need your reconciliation team to map sums for revenue recognition.

Next steps: I can scope a small PR to Billing to expose the flags and a console toggle. ETA: 2 sprints for core flags + 1 supplementary sprint for invoice PDF templates.

Ben Carter
Billing Product Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Oliver James <oliver.james@arcadia-retail.com>

Appreciate the clear plan — a few follow-ups from our side:
1) Audit evidence: can Redwood provide exportable validation logs (immutable) that we can keep for auditors? A copy per invoice/settlement would be ideal.
2) Attestation: will Redwood sign a short attestation confirming we ran the validations (a 1–2 paragraph statement)? Our auditors prefer a signed statement for the year-end.
3) Collection hold duration: 7 business days sounds reasonable, but can we increase to 30 days for high-risk sellers while still getting a notification stream?
4) Revenue recognition: will delayed payout mean Redwood reports the gross revenue differently? We need to coordinate with our accountant.

CC'd our external tax advisor Maya Singh on the thread for any regulatory corner cases she sees. If it's helpful, we can run a joint call Thursday.

Thanks,
Oliver

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 11:04:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: VAT handling for marketplace sellers - data attached

Oliver / team — quick compliance summary from Legal: 

- Reverse charge applicability: In the EU, reverse-charge treatment for B2B cross-border supplies is contingent on a valid VAT ID for the supplier (seller). Without a validated VAT ID, the platform should charge VAT and not apply reverse charge.
- Validation evidence: VIES responses are acceptable evidence for auditors but we should preserve the raw response, timestamp, and the query parameters. For added assurance, maintain an audit trail that ties VIES results to the invoice/settlement id.
- Attestation: Redwood can provide a one-off attestation cover letter stating we performed validations according to agreed process and retained logs. We will need to define scope and a signature owner (Legal + Product).
- Holds and accounting: Holding payouts does not change the VAT liability on the invoice itself — it changes settlement timing. Arcadia should coordinate with its accountant on revenue recognition. We will add invoice-level notes such as "Pending VAT validation - settlement on hold" to support your auditors.

Proposed SLA: Redwood will attempt automated validation within 24 hours and complete manual review within 7 business days; for exceptions (suspected fraud/high risk) we can escalate to 30 days with documented steps. If that SLA works, we'll include it in the attestation and the service addendum.

I'll draft the attestation language and share a template for your review.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
